# ADR trigger notes — R4.7a (2026-10-22)

Re-homed fired-trigger records (landed ADR bodies are frozen — BM-ADR-01;
precedent 0b3ca91 / R4.5 repair 94a0653). Sources: the R4.7a run ledger
(`docs/build/runs/R4.7a.md`) is the narrative home.

## ADR-0351 — revisit trigger clause 1: FIRED

Trigger text: *"Reopen when a ticket lands a TLS-terminating transport
or a real OAuth provider leg (BL-31 — `mtls` gains its handshake's
peer-identity map and `oauth` gains a provider challenge→token
exchange…)"*

R4.7a lands both, exactly as the trigger anticipated:

- **Real OAuth provider leg** — `crates/hh-mcp-lab/src/oauth.rs`: the
  GitHub OAuth-App device flow (device code → user verification → token
  poll with `authorization_pending`/`slow_down`/`expired_token`/
  `access_denied`/`incorrect_device_code` → `GET /user` subject) plus
  the mediator's bearer→subject verify (`OAuthIssuer::verify_bearer`).
  `LabServer.oauth_issuers` is the declared issuer table: a declared
  `issuer_ref` verifies through the provider exchange; an undeclared
  one keeps the landed kernel `minted_scoped` leg (D5's path is
  untouched — the `issuer:test`-style grants in r2_19 resolve
  identically). Typed refusals: forged → `credential_invalid`,
  provider-unreachable → `issuer_unreachable` (new additive
  `CredentialRefusal` variant, CC8 — transient no-answer, distinct from
  `transport_absent`'s no-exchange-exists).
- **TLS-terminating transport + peer-identity map** —
  `hh_mcp_lab::http::serve_http_mtls` terminates TLS via
  `ServerTls::requiring_client_auth`; the handshake's verified
  `PeerIdentity` resolves through the declared `mtls_subjects`
  subject→binding table (`resolve_mtls_peer`; CN → SAN-URI → SAN-DNS
  key order). `transport_absent` remains only where TLS is not
  configured (the plain HTTP arm) — matching the trigger's condition.

Consumption note (ADR-0365 D3 adjacency): `hh-mcp-lab` consumes
`hh_tls` types through `hh_embed::service` re-exports — the D5
`MintedVerdict` precedent applied to the TLS surface set — so D3's
closed consumer list (`hh-gateway`, `hh-env`, `hh-embed`) is literally
unchanged; no sibling ADR required, no second crate names the admitted
graph. `ServerTlsStream::set_nonblocking` was added inside `hh-tls`'s
own API (multiplex-arm support).

## ADR-0303 — revisit trigger (b): FIRED

Trigger text: *"…(b) the H3 credential mediator resolves oauth/mtls
bindings (DF-S4.11-2)…"*

Fired by the same landing: `oauth` bindings now resolve through the
declared-issuer provider exchange (or the kernel minted leg), and
`mtls` bindings resolve through the TLS handshake's verified peer
identity → declared subject map — both producing the same
`CallerBinding` the stdio path yields; bogus credentials answer
`401`/typed refusal, never a guessed subject. The serial-turn model is
unchanged — trigger clause (d) untouched.

## What R4.7a does NOT do to the ADRs

- ADR-0351 D5's kernel-owned verdict seam stands: `MintedVerdict` still
  verifies kernel-minted tokens; the provider exchange is the
  *addition* the trigger named, not a replacement.
- `oauth{audience}` bindings with undeclared `issuer_ref`s behave
  byte-identically (back-compat — the grant-table → credential-kind
  mediation order is unchanged).
- No landed ADR body edited; these notes ride the report + run ledger
  only.
